title: Time difference between 1 January 1970 and now
description:
Calculate the time difference between 1 January 1970 and now.

Python-Gym adaptation: reading the live clock would make the expected result non-deterministic, so implement as time_since_epoch(now), taking a fixed datetime.datetime object now instead of the real current time, and returning the timedelta between 1 January 1970 (midnight) and now.
starter_code:
import datetime

def time_since_epoch(now):
    # your code here
    pass
hints: Subtracting one datetime object from another gives you a timedelta representing the difference between them.
The reference point '1 January 1970' can be built directly with datetime.datetime(1970, 1, 1).
Construct epoch = datetime.datetime(1970, 1, 1) and return now - epoch.
expected_behavior: Given a fixed 'now' datetime, returns the timedelta elapsed since midnight of 1 January 1970.
solution:
import datetime

def time_since_epoch(now):
    epoch = datetime.datetime(1970, 1, 1)
    return now - epoch

hidden_tests.label: time elapsed from epoch to the very next day

explanation: Subtracting one datetime.datetime from another produces a datetime.timedelta representing the elapsed time between them. Using datetime.datetime(1970, 1, 1) as the reference point mirrors the well-known Unix epoch used throughout computing.
